requirement:
`habeas status` MUST group the selected requirement and example judgments marked
FIXME by issue reference and report how many distinct judgments each issue
affects. A recorded FIXME string of the form `owner/repo#N` under
{cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes` MUST identify that issue, compared exactly; any
other string is a gap description without an issue.

A judgment MUST count at most once for each issue, even when that issue occurs
repeatedly or in several FIXME strings. A judgment naming several issues MUST
count in each corresponding group. Judgments with no issue string MUST be counted once in a separate "FIXME without an issue" group.
Issue groups MUST be ordered by decreasing affected-judgment count, then by
reference; the group without an issue MUST follow them. A supplied
selection MUST restrict these counts to the selected subjects.

`--verbose` MUST list the full name and kind of every judgment in each issue
group and in the group without an issue, along with its original FIXME strings.
The summary MUST include valid FIXME determinations even when other evidence
checks fail; grouping MUST NOT hide their validation findings. Malformed
determinations MUST remain validation errors under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Each obligation has code reachable from the `{impl}` items and a test that runs that code.

**Reachability.** `src/main.rs#fn[main]` carries the `{impl}` for the `Status` command. It calls `status_markdown_with_github`, which the `{impl}`-marked `src/commands.rs#fn[status_markdown]` reaches through its filtered variant. That function collects entries with `fixmes.add(name, kind, evidence.fixme_entries())` for each non-term definition that matches the selection glob. It renders the result with `FixmeSummary::render(verbose)` in `src/fixme.rs`. `LoadedDetailEvidence::load_path` in `src/index.rs` supplies the entries. Everything below is reached from these items, so none of it needs its own reference.

**Obligations, code and tests**

| Obligation | Code | Tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Group selected judgments by issue and report distinct-judgment counts | `FixmeSummary::render` groups into a `BTreeMap` and prints `affects N judgment(s)` | `tests/commands.rs#fn[status_groups_fixme_judgments_by_distinct_exact_issue]`; `src/fixme.rs` tests `groups_order_by_decreasing_count_before_reference` and `verbose_output_lists_each_judgment_under_every_group_it_belongs_to` |
| An `owner/repo#N` string identifies the issue, compared exactly; any other string is a gap description | `issue_references` and `is_issue_reference` use an anchored regex and a `BTreeSet`; comparison is case-sensitive | `only_exact_issue_references_identify_issues` (URL, `FIXME(...)`, prose, `#7` and leading zeros all name no issue); the commands test, where `Rust-Lang/rust#456` and `rust-lang/rust#456` are separate groups |
| Count a judgment at most once per issue, including repeats and several strings | `BTreeSet` deduplication in `issue_references` | `verbose_output_...` uses `["o/r#1","o/r#2","o/r#1"]` and checks `o/r#1` affects 2 judgments |
| A judgment naming several issues counts in each group | The loop pushes the judgment into every issue's group | `rules.both` appears under both `o/r#1` and `o/r#2` |
| Judgments with no issue go in a separate "FIXME without an issue" group, counted once | `without_issue` vector, rendered as `N judgment(s) marked FIXME without an issue` | The `only_exact...` test and the commands tests |
| Order by decreasing count, then reference; the no-issue group follows | `sort_by(right.len().cmp(&left.len()).then(a.cmp(b)))`; the no-issue line is rendered after the issue lines | `groups_order_by_decreasing_count_before_reference`; the commands test checks the no-issue line comes after the last issue group |
| A selection restricts the counts | The glob filter in `status_markdown_with_github` runs before `fixmes.add` | `verbose_status_lists_fixme_judgments_and_globs_scope_issue_groups` checks `rules.case` and `rules.unlinked` show only their own groups |
| `--verbose` lists the full name, kind and original FIXME strings for every issue group and the no-issue group | `render_judgments` prints `` `name` (kind) `` and an escaped `<pre>` block of the original entries | `verbose_output_...` and the verbose commands test (HTML escaping, original strings, requirement and example kinds) |
| Include valid FIXME determinations even when other checks fail; grouping must not hide validation findings | `load_path` derives `fixme_entries` from the parsed judgment regardless of validation errors. The `Validation findings` sections are still emitted separately | `tests/outcomes.rs#fn[fixme_does_not_hide_stale_inputs_or_uncovered_references]` shows the row is `Invalid`, `example/io#125` still appears, and `outline input changed` still appears |
| Malformed determinations remain validation errors | `Judgment::from_value` fails, so no entries are added and the validator reports the error | `tests/outcomes.rs#fn[malformed_fixme_is_invalid_and_reports_the_required_shape]` shows `Invalid`, the `nonempty array` message, and no `affects` line |

Each of these tests carries a `{test}` reference to `requirements.cli.fixme_summary`. The remaining test, `tests/outcomes.rs#fn[valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book]`, covers non-verbose and `--all` runs and a verbose run.

**Unspecified behavior.** The `## FIXME judgments` heading, the singular/plural wording and the `<pre>` rendering are layout and wording choices within what the text describes. I found no extra behavior that needs a separate specification.

A judgment MUST count at most once for each issue, even when that issue occurs
repeatedly or in several FIXME strings. A judgment naming several issues MUST

Issue groups MUST be ordered by decreasing affected-judgment count, then by

`--verbose` MUST list the full name and kind of every judgment in each issue

:::{req} outcomes
Every assessment judgment MUST use one of these outcomes, applying
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`:
- `true`: the sources support the subject and its testing obligations.
- `false`: the sources do not support the subject, or information is missing,
and the gaps are not all acknowledged by `{fixme}` references to it.
- `FIXME`: some aspects remain unmet or untested, and `{fixme}` references to
the subject acknowledge every one of those gaps. The reviewer MUST explain the
gaps and their source locations in the rationale and record their issue
references or other identifying content from the inputs.
The JSON `determination` MUST be `true`, `false`, or an object containing exactly
`"FIXME"` with a nonempty array of nonempty strings, such as
`{"FIXME": ["example/queue#125", "rust-lang/rust#123"]}`. A gap MUST count as
acknowledged only by a `{fixme}` reference under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` whose body describes that gap and that
references the assessed definition, or, for a site review, the distributed requirement from within that site; a citation review MUST NOT accept a `{fixme}`; a plain
`FIXME` comment, another marker such as `TODO`, or prose MUST NOT. The strings
MUST list each distinct issue reference the acknowledging `{fixme}` references
name in their option lines, as written after `:github:`, and, for a `{fixme}`
naming no issue, its body's words, without comment delimiters, joined by single
spaces. A `{fixme}` reference describing a gap that no longer exists MUST itself
be treated as a gap. A `{fixme}` naming a GitHub issue that
{cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads` reports closed MUST NOT count as
acknowledging its gap. A FIXME judgment MUST be grounded in recorded evidence
inputs.
